selection: The five most recently published stable versions of each named package before the cutoff, ordered by npm publication timestamp; evaluate all four adjacent transitions, including unchanged descriptors and acquisition failures.

independent_comparator.endpoint: All reported descriptor changes, with severity preserved. A compatibility-breaking decision is not equated with a reapproval decision.

capture.environment: Explicit non-secret environment allowlist; no browser launch, account, credentials or production data. Runtime package installation disables lifecycle scripts.

questions: Can an ordinary local tools/list capture and offline comparison be reproduced from pinned released packages?
Which actual changed fields receive policy findings, and which changes are absent from the baseline lint report?
Does an independently implemented current comparator already expose the same review evidence?
What useful scope remains for a compact public artifact?
decision: Prepare a small experimental artifact only if the results support a clear practical use. Do not expand standalone-product or human-study infrastructure. A useful casebook or honest limitations result is an acceptable outcome; no useful difference is an acceptable stop outcome.
limits: No independent approval labels or human review measurements; no accuracy or review-time claims.
Five packages from three publisher families, including three correlated packages from one repository; no ecosystem prevalence inference.
Capture dependencies are frozen at acquisition, not necessarily identical to the dependencies resolved on the original publication date.
tools/list is metadata evidence, not evidence of runtime tool behavior.
Any later policy fixes are evaluated separately; this sample cannot subsequently be called an untouched holdout.
